methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Maglut Heavy Industries is a pre-seed robotics and manufacturing company founded by Azhar Yerzhanova and Curtis Wu. The broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector contains one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median approach is not applicable to this valuation. The filtering criteria—same stage, adjacent stage, and similar valuation tier—yielded fewer than three datapoints despite ten same-sector peers existing in the Robotics & Manufacturing universe. Applying an all-sector median would introduce excessive noise given the stage and capital requirements specific to frontier robotics development. No triangulated valuation range can be derived from comparable company analysis alone.

At the pre-seed stage with no reported prior fundraising, Maglut lacks sufficient operating history to support revenue or EBITDA multiples. Forward-looking methods (DCF, option pricing) would require unreliable assumptions about development timelines and market adoption. The founding team's relevant experience—Yerzhanova's strategy and analytics background alongside Wu's exposure to manufacturing, pharma, and defense—provides some technical and operational credibility but does not bridge the absence of financial or transactional comps. A meaningful valuation would require either identifying sufficiently similar seed-stage robotics companies with disclosed terms or employing venture-capital cost-of-capital methods, neither of which is supported by the available data. Professional judgment on funding offer terms and market conditions at time of close remains essential.
